housingAlert: Never pay a deposit or rent before you have seen the room (in person or on a live video call) and signed a contract.
Be wary of prices far below the area average, landlords who are 'abroad' and can only send keys by courier, and requests to pay by wire transfer to a private account or via money-transfer apps.
Ask for the landlord's ID and check that the contract will be registered. Keep every receipt.
Ask your university's international office or the PoliTo Students community before paying anything.

tasks.title: University pre-enrolment (Universitaly)
tasks.description: Non-EU students apply through the Universitaly 'Pre-enrolment' procedure. The chosen institution issues a letter of eligibility for enrolment, which the embassy or consulate needs for the study visa.
documentsNeeded: Admission or exchange acceptance from the Italian institution
steps: Create an account on Universitaly
Submit the pre-enrolment application for your institution
Wait for the institution's letter of eligibility
tasks.cost: Not stated on the official page

tasks.title: Study visa (type D)
tasks.description: Non-EU students apply for a national (type D) study visa at the Italian embassy or consulate in their country of residence, using the letter of eligibility from Universitaly. The Italian Foreign Ministry portal has a guided check of whether you need a visa.
steps: Check visa requirement on the Foreign Ministry visa portal
Book an appointment at the Italian embassy or consulate
Submit the application and collect the visa
tasks.officialSourceName: Il visto per l'Italia – Ministero degli Affari Esteri
tasks.cost: Not stated on the pages checked
tasks.todo: Visa fee and the consulate's document list are not verified.

tasks.title: Health insurance (EHIC)
tasks.description: EU citizens use the European Health Insurance Card for medically necessary care during a temporary stay. It is free and you request it from your own health insurer before leaving. It does not cover private care, mountain rescue or repatriation, so consider a complementary policy.
steps: Request the EHIC from your health insurer before you travel
Check the validity dates cover your whole stay
Decide whether you need extra private cover
tasks.officialSourceName: Your Europe – Health cover for temporary stays
tasks.cost: Free (avoid websites that charge for it)

tasks.title: Health insurance (non-EU)
tasks.description: Non-EU students need health cover for their stay; it is usually checked for the visa and the residence permit. The exact options (private policy or voluntary registration with the national health service) still have to be verified with an official source.
steps: Ask your consulate which cover is accepted for the visa
Keep the policy for the residence-permit appointment

tasks.title: Accommodation
tasks.description: Find a room or flat and sign a contract. You will need the address for the municipal registration and, for non-EU students, for the residence permit. Housing scams are the most common problem students report: read the alert before paying anything.
steps: Shortlist offers (university housing office, verified platforms)
View the room or do a live video call
Sign the contract and keep every receipt

tasks.title: University documents & arrival check-in
tasks.description: Complete your exchange paperwork with the host university (learning agreement, arrival registration with the international office, student card). Each university publishes its own list.
steps: Sign the learning agreement with both universities
Check in at the international office on arrival
Collect your student card and credentials

tasks.title: Italian tax code
tasks.description: The codice fiscale is the Italian tax identification number. For a first codice fiscale you book an in-person appointment at an Agenzia delle Entrate office. Non-EU citizens can also get it at the Sportello Unico per l'immigrazione or a Questura, and must show a passport with visa or a residence permit.
documentsNeeded: Non-EU: passport with visa or residence permit
steps: Book an appointment at an Agenzia delle Entrate office
Bring your ID and the request form
Keep the certificate: phone lines, banks and contracts will ask for it
tasks.officialSourceName: Agenzia delle Entrate – Tax identification number for foreign citizens
tasks.cost: Not stated on the official page

tasks.title: Residence permit for study
tasks.localName: Permesso di soggiorno per motivi di studio
tasks.description: Within 8 working days of arriving on a type D study visa, book an appointment to apply for the permesso di soggiorno for study at the Questura (Ufficio stranieri). The visa portal states the same 8-working-day deadline for stays over 90 days.

extraSources.name: Il visto per l'Italia – Ministero degli Affari Esteri

steps: Within 8 working days of arrival, book the appointment
Attend the Questura appointment
Collect the permit when ready
tasks.estimatedTime: Several weeks until the permit is issued
tasks.cost: Not stated on the pages checked
tasks.deadline: Apply within 8 working days of arrival

tasks.title: Municipal registration
tasks.description: EU citizens staying more than 3 months register with the Anagrafe of their municipality; the host country cannot require it during the first 3 months. In Turin, after moving into a new home the residence declaration must be filed with the Anagrafe within 20 days.

extraSources.name: Your Europe – Students abroad in the EU: residence right

steps: Book an appointment with the Anagrafe
File the residence declaration with your documents
Keep the receipt; the municipality may check your address
tasks.cost: Not stated on the official page
tasks.deadline: Residence declaration within 20 days of moving (Turin)

tasks.title: Leisure & life in Turin: transport pass

Buy it online or at a sales point
Explore the City tab for places near you

Cancel utilities and subscriptions in your name
